findings.text: GRANDFATHERING RESIDUAL ESCAPE (bounded, honest, deferred; not blocking). module_lines binds only GOVERNED files (files that resolve to a declared contract area). Because the contracts/loop/fleet/metrics/tracker/distribution areas enumerate EXACT file paths (not globs), a brand-new over-budget module placed at a NEW path in one of those areas (e.g. .warp/newbig.py) resolves to no area and is therefore ungoverned by any budget. I reproduced this: a 2000-line .warp/newbig.py in the change set is NOT refused, while a 1500-line new file under the runners/** GLOB area IS refused. This is not a W2 dodge and does not make the budget toothless: (a) the budget is fully toothed over the change class it claims (governed files, including new files in glob-covered areas and any governed file grown/changed past budget); (b) the path cannot be added silently, since footprint-versus-diff refuses a touched path a spec did not declare; (c) closing the escape belongs to W1 contract completeness (enumerate the engine modules or use area globs, a gap WARP-1104 already flagged for the placeless siblings decision_review.py/decision.py/tripwire.py/shape_review.py) plus the explicitly-deferred new-module detection, not to this gate. Recommend the contract be tightened in a later item so every engine module is governed; it does not affect this item's soundness, green-safety, or tier.

LIVE ENFORCEMENT SCOPE IS THE HONEST READING OF 'MECHANIZABLE', NOT A DODGE. O2's prose lists dependency/boundary, size, complexity, duplication, and pattern violations as gate failures; today only module_lines and the three engine invariants are gate-BLOCKING because those are the only rules THIS repository's contract marks enforcement: mechanizable (authored and founder-approved in W1). The boundary/function-length/duplication/complexity analyzers are shipped and I proved each detects a seeded violation and BLOCKS the instant its rule is relabeled mechanizable; keeping them in the review lane behind the contract label is the correct NG5 posture, not toothlessness. If a reviewer expected all of O2's classes to be red checks in THIS repo today, that expectation is met only after the contract flips those labels (a founder decision), which is by design.

adoption_safe_fail_closed is wired to an EMPTY enforcement tuple: it is embodied by the gate's own stand-down code path rather than an external catalog check, so prose_enforcement_findings always returns clean for it as long as it stays registered. This is honest (documented in the module and the manifest) and non-vacuous (the behavior is real and proven by selftest AC2, which would go red if the stand-down were removed), but it is worth noting that this one mechanizable rule's 'enforcement' is guaranteed by the selftest rather than by a deletion-detecting catalog-file check like its siblings.
